headline: Deferred review of 179 Queen City Park Road pre-treatment facility addition to 11/17/26; other projects were heard but not decided.
summary: The board heard a conditional use request for home catering and take-out at 28 Janet Circle and a request to extend a planting deadline at 451 Appletree Point Road. Neighbors raised traffic and smoke concerns about the catering proposal. The only recorded vote was to defer the 179 Queen City Park Road item to 11/17/26.
decisions: Deferred the 179 Queen City Park Road pre-treatment facility addition to 11/17/26, vote 5-0.

decision_evidence.quote: Geoff Hand: Motioned to defer this item to the 11/17/26 DRB meeting, Chase Taylor 2nd. Vote 5-0. Motion carried.

BURLINGTON DEVELOPMENT REVIEW BOARD 
Tuesday, October 20, 2026, 5:00 PM 
 
MINTES 
 
 Hybrid & In Person (at 645 Pine Street) Meeting 
 
Board Members Present: Evan Gould, Geoff Hand (5:15 PM), Sean McKenzie, Chase Taylor, and Marina 
Campbell 
 
Board Members Absent: Caitlin Halpert and Miles Waite 
 
Staff Members Present: Scott Gustin, Mary O’Neil, and Joseph Cava 
 
Staff Members Absent: Kirk Dressing and Matthew Clark  
 
I. Agenda 
II. Communications 
III. Minutes 
IV. Public Hearing 
 
1. ZP-26-432; 28 Janet Circle (RL, Ward 7) Indra Rai / Bidur Rai   
Conditional use for home catering and take-out business. (Project Manager, Mary O’Neil) 
Bidur Rai, owner, present, Johanna Schneider, Marilyn Hill, Marcia Robair, and Ali Dieng: Sworn 
in. 
 
Evan Gould: Can you tell us about this project? 
 
Bidur Rai: I started working when I came here in 2009. When my Mom moved here, I quit my job to 
stay home and take care of her. My goal is to establish a home occupation so I can continue to work. 
 
Johanna Schneider: Bidur was referred to me by another individual operating a home occupation in 
the New North End. We have been organizing, doing prep work, since August to get this proposal 
operational.  
 
Evan Gould: Are there any questions or comments from members of the Board?  
 
Sean McKenzie: How many visits per day? 
 
Johanna Schneider: Wednesday evenings between 4:30 PM and 7:30 PM. Our goal for revenue is to 
establish five to ten takeout orders.  
 
Evan Gould: Does the website have staged pick up times? 
 
Johanna Schneider: We are working on it.
Sean McKenzie: From the project plans, there would be one parking spot on street and two in the 
driveway.  
 
Johanna Schneider: Yes, we are working on it.  
 
Marilyn Hill: I have a petition from the following neighbors of Janet Circle. We are a small artery 
off of James Avenue. The only people who drive in this neighborhood are residents. I am concerned 
that business traffic will generate 30-40 cars coming in and out of the neighborhood. On another 
nearby street, food scraps had led to rat infestation. I have Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease 
(COPD), and smoke generated from another catering businesses has led negative health 
consequences. What is the timeframe, days in operation and hours of operation? If people are 
coming to pick up orders while others are waiting, how will the excess traffic be regulated? People 
buy houses in this neighborhood because it is quiet. Children play in the street because it is safe.  
 
Marcia Robair: How will the children be protected from the additional, incoming traffic? 
 
Marilyn Hill: How can a business be profitable in such a small area? I like my neighbors and I get 
along with them. These are good neighbors, and I do not oppose the proposal, just not in our 
neighborhood.  
 
Marcia Robair: We have not had a problem with our neighbors for over twenty years. I am 
concerned the impact traffic will have on children playing in the street.  
 
Evan Gould: Are there any conditions you would like us to impose on this project? 
 
Marilyn Hill: Neighbors congregate between my house and the neighbor’s house.  
 
Geoff Hand: I appreciate the neighborhood prospective, but we are limited to the regulations 
outlined in the Comprehensive Development Ordinance (CDO) regarding our review of this project. 
 
Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the public attending 
in person or present online?  
 
Ali Dieng: My house is off of Janet Circle on James Avenue. Bidur wants to do work to support his 
family and he is not asking for help. This type of project should be celebrated. The catering business 
is the only option he has. I only heard about this project through neighboring opposition. 
 
Marilyn Hill: I have nothing to do with this.  
 
Ali Dieng: I, myself, have tried to resolve a similar problem.  
 
Marilyn Hill: I have not victimized anyone.  
 
Evan Gould: There should not be any back and forth between meeting participants. We are here to 
listen on this project’s applicability to the CDO.  
 
Ali Dieng: I do not think a catering business will generate the type of traffic being projected by 
neighboring opposition.  
 
Evan Gould: I would like to hear from the applicant.  
 
Bidur Rai: Words spoken in anger should not be considered. I am here to freely operate a business to 
help support my family.
Geoff Hand: So to clarify, are you using a smoker for this business? 
 
Bidur Rai: No 
 
Evan Gould: Would you be amendable to conditions on hours of operation?  
 
Bidur Rai: The first time I saw the smoke in the neighborhood, I asked if they needed help.  
 
Evan Gould: I appreciate the context, but this is unrelated to the main issues. The two issues I have 
heard before us are traffic generation and smoke.  
 
Johanna Schneider: We are working on scheduling with the website.  
 
Geoff Hand: People pick up take out across the street from me all the time. I have no issue with this.  
 
Marilyn Hill: I like my neighbor, but… 
 
Evan Gould: We are not here to engage with neighboring disputes or drama.  
 
Bidur Rai: There have been many issues directed at my family in this neighborhood.  
 
Evan Gould: Hearing no additional questions or comments, we will close the hearing on this item to 
deliberate on it later on.  
 
V. Certificate of Appropriateness 
 
1. ZP-26-334; 179 Queen City Park Road (E-LM, Ward 5) Zoo Holdings, LLC / Martin 
Courcelle 
Proposed construction of pre-treatment facility addition including associated site and utility 
improvements. (Project Manager, Kirk Dressing)  
 
Evan Gould: Is the applicant present? 
 
Scott Gustin: The applicant has requested that this item be deferred.  
 
Evan Gould: Would someone like to make a motion? 
 
Geoff Hand: Motioned to defer this item to the 11/17/26 DRB meeting, Chase Taylor 2nd. Vote 5-0. 
Motion carried. 
 
2. ZP-26-455; 451 Appletree Point Road (RL, Ward 4) Jamie Spano  
Modify Project Permit Condition 1 of zoning permit, ZP-25-378, to allow additional time to 
complete the project. (Project Manager, Scott Gustin) 
Keith McManis: Sworn in.  
 
Evan Gould: Is the applicant present? 
 
Keith McManis: Yes. 
 
Evan Gould: Can you tell us about this project? 
 
Keith McManis: We seek to extend the deadline beyond what was previously approved. 
 
Sean McKenzie: So the new deadline for plantings would be 9/15/27 instead?
Geoff Hand: My understanding is that this was a retroactive permit for work that was already 
completed. Now that you are waiting to continue with replanting, it will be costlier to you than if it 
were completed by this year’s deadline. There was a specific timeframe to comply. If we do not 
accept the time extension, what does this mean? 
 
Scott Gustin: There is a subsection for compliance under the CDO.  
 
Geoff Hand: Will back penalties be applied for the original violation? 
 
Scott Gustin: It can definitely be reviewed for consideration.  
 
Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? 
 
Marina Campbell: Do we need to approve a later time, or could we have an earlier check in like 
March or April? 
 
Keith McManis: March would be too early for plantings, but having a contract in place could be 
helpful to ensure it will be underway.  
 
Evan Gould: Hearing no additional questions or comments from the Board, are there any questions 
or comments from members of the public attending in person or present online? Hearing none, we 
will close the hearing on this item to deliberate on this evening’s agenda items. 
 
VI. Adjournment 
Hearing closed at 5:50 PM.
